expectations.text: Both skill and agent created (a pair)
expectations.evidence: Two agents were authored (.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md lead + repo-scout.md investigator — an agent+agent pair), but no repo-triage skill was created. The only skill under home/.agents/skills/ is omp-setup/SKILL.md, byte-identical (sha256 117a7ad80e82…, re-verified) to the pre-existing canonical omp-setup skill — a copy of an existing skill, not a created one, and not paired with the agent: omp-setup never references repo-triage, and delegation is wired agent→agent via `spawns: repo-scout`, not skill→agent.

expectations.text: Agent frontmatter includes autoloadSkills naming omp-setup
expectations.evidence: repo-triage.md frontmatter: `autoloadSkills:` (list) containing `- omp-setup`; the field is real (omp://task-agent-discovery.md:47) and both scalar and list forms appear in omp docs/examples.

expectations.text: Agent at home/.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md, skill at home/.agents/skills/
expectations.evidence: Verified on disk: outputs/.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md and a skill at outputs/.agents/skills/omp-setup/SKILL.md. Paths are literally correct; note the skill is the copied canonical omp-setup, not an authored repo-triage skill (penalized under assertion 1/4, not here).

expectations.text: Skill spells out the task-tool delegation contract
expectations.evidence: The only skill present is the verbatim canonical omp-setup SKILL.md, which covers provisioning/config conventions and contains no task-tool delegation contract (no agent to spawn, no context/task split). The delegation contract exists but lives in the agent file's '# Partner contract' section ('Batch independent dives into a single task call with agent: "repo-scout"'), not in a skill. No authored skill spells out the contract.

expectations.text: Agent has one-job statement and anti-jobs
expectations.evidence: repo-triage.md lead: single-deliverable one-job statement — 'return ONE structured triage report as your final message — that message is the deliverable the requesting session receives'. Anti-jobs in substance under '# Guardrails': 'Read-only on the target repo: no edits, writes, deletes, installs, or network fetches', 'A claim without evidence is a hypothesis', 'never end with a plan, a question, or a promise of follow-up work' (last one in the opening paragraph).

claims.claim: Installed omp-setup copied verbatim, sha256-verified byte-identical to canonical
claims.evidence: Re-verified: sha256 117a7ad80e82f6cc826c482d62d12b7e23819b44a34495143eb1a0f256eab59d matches both /home/x20/.agents/skills/omp-setup/SKILL.md and skills/omp-setup/SKILL.md.

claims.claim: autoloadSkills is omp's supported preload mechanism; unknown names are silently ignored
claims.evidence: omp://task-agent-discovery.md:47: 'autoloadSkills names skills from the parent session to inject before the first child prompt; unknown names are ignored'; omp://slash-command-internals.md:562 concurs.

claims.claim: Subagent sessions inherit the discovered skills list, so repo-scout can resolve skill://omp-setup on demand instead of carrying the injection
claims.evidence: omp://skills.md:168: 'Task tool subagents receive the session's discovered/provided skills list via normal session creation.'

claims.claim: The pair needs task.maxRecursionDepth ≥ 2, which the default-profile default suffices for
claims.evidence: Pair nests two levels (session→repo-triage→repo-scout); omp://slash-command-internals.md:563 documents task removal at max recursion depth, so the ≥2 requirement is consistent with documented behavior. The exact default value was not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: repo-scout has no task tool, so nesting stops there
claims.evidence: Scout frontmatter `tools: read,grep,glob,find,bash` — no task; `spawns` omitted.

claims.claim: A two-agent pair plus an omp-setup skill copy satisfies the user's 'agent pair' ask
claims.evidence: The extra artifacts (second agent, copied skill) are internally consistent and omp-documented, but the eval defines the pair as an authored skill + agent wired via the task tool; graded strictly per assertions 1 and 4, which this architecture fails.

suggestions.assertion: Both skill and agent created (a pair)
suggestions.reason: Ambiguous: 'pair' reads as two agents in the user's prompt ('an omp agent pair'), and the baseline half-passes any literal reading (a skill file does exist at home/.agents/skills/, agents exist). Tighten to: 'an authored repo-triage SKILL.md exists whose body names and spawns the repo-triage agent via the task tool' — that wording separates genuine pair creation from a skill copy plus agent-agent wiring.

suggestions.assertion: Agent at home/.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md, skill at home/.agents/skills/
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating on its own: copying any skill into home/.agents/skills/ satisfies it, as this run demonstrated. Fold a content check into it or drop it in favor of assertions 2/4.

suggestions.assertion: Skill spells out the task-tool delegation contract
suggestions.reason: This is the most discriminating assertion in the set — it is exactly where the baseline's no-skill architecture fails. Keep it, and consider also asserting the contract appears in the skill (not the agent), since this run moved the contract into the agent's '# Partner contract' section.

No coverage for functional preload resolution: neither run is checked on whether the autoloaded skill is actually discoverable (this run installed it; the with_skill run did not verify). An assertion that 'the skill named in autoloadSkills resolves under home/.agents/skills/' would credit the genuinely useful extra step observed here.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertion 4 cleanly discriminates; assertions 1 and 3 leak passes to a copy-instead-of-author strategy, and the eval never checks preload resolvability or agent tool discipline.
